messages:
sam: flagging a reproducible bug: SDK prefetch + transport retries can surface duplicate items to apps. reproduced on python/ts.
rachel: is the SDK doing optimistic prefetches of the next page and the transport is transparently retrying failed requests?
hiro: yep. prefetch triggers an inflight request. if transport retries, server can return same page twice and iterator yields dupes.
leah: we have three knobs: (1) let iterator dedupe items (client-side), (2) make cursor fetches idempotent via client idempotency key, (3) teach transport to treat prefetch as non-retriable.
sam: tradeoffs?
rachel: (1) is heavy for long streams and changes iterator semantics; (2) is correct but needs server/contract work; (3) is minimal and can be rolled out quickly but means prefetch may fail silently and waste opportunity.
hiro: proposal: add a small transport hint header `X-Redwood-Prefetch: 1` plus a `X-Redwood-Session` id. Transport sees the header and suppresses automatic retries for those requests. SDKs generate a session-id per iterator.
leah: language ergonomics: python/ts keep prefetch on by default but opt-in to session headers only when server feature-flag is on; go exposes a context opt-in. hide idempotency tokens from users.
sam: observability: emit metric `prefetch.suppressed_retries` and `prefetch.duplicate_detected` to detect regressions.
hiro: test plan: inject transient 500s on prefetch path and assert no duplicates across py/ts/go interop tests. also test scenario where server honors idempotency header in a follow-up phase.
ops-bot: note: server-side change should be feature-flagged; SDKs ship the header opt-in behind a toggle.
leah: I'll draft a short follow-up RFC and example snippets for each SDK. assigning sam + hiro to transport/server pieces.
